title: Make and scale a vector
body: Make a vector x with the numbers 1 through 26, then multiply it by 2 and print it.
hint: 1:26 makes the sequence; arithmetic on a vector applies to every element.

title: Mean and standard deviation
body:
Print the mean and the standard deviation of x, each rounded to 2 decimals.

[1] 14.5
[1] 4.85
solution:
x <- c(12, 15, 9, 22, 18, 11)
print(round(mean(x), 2))
print(round(sd(x), 2))
hint: round(mean(x), 2), round(sd(x), 2), each inside print().

title: Name a vector
body: Make a vector letter_no with the numbers 1 to 26 and set its names to the built-in LETTERS. Then show letter_no["B"], which should give 2.
solution:
letter_no <- 1:26
names(letter_no) <- LETTERS
letter_no["B"]
hint: names(x) <- LETTERS.

title: Two ways to subset
body:
Given the named vector x, write two different commands that each return elements b, c and d:

  b   c   d
6.2 7.1 4.8
hint: Positions work (x[2:4]), so do negative positions that drop elements, and names.

title: Filter with a condition
body: Return the values in x that are greater than 4 and less than 7.
hint: Combine two logical conditions with & inside the brackets.

title: Dig into a list
body: Using list and vector subsetting, extract the number 2 from xlist. (It is inside the b item.)
starter: xlist <- list(a = "Software Carpentry", b = 1:10, data = head(mtcars))
solution:
xlist <- list(a = "Software Carpentry", b = 1:10, data = head(mtcars))
xlist$b[2]
hint: xlist$b (or xlist[["b"]]) gives the vector; then index it.

title: Match against a list
body:
Produce a logical vector that is TRUE for every country in countries that is in Southeast Asia (seAsia) and FALSE otherwise. Then use it to print the matching countries.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
seAsia <- c("Myanmar", "Thailand", "Cambodia", "Vietnam", "Laos")
countries <- unique(gapminder$country)
in_sea <- countries %in% seAsia
countries[in_sea]
hint: countries == seAsia recycles and gives the wrong answer. %in% checks membership.

title: Matrix indexing
body: Extract the values 11 and 14 from the matrix m using row and column indices.
solution:
m <- matrix(1:18, nrow = 3, ncol = 6)
m[2, c(4, 5)]
hint: Matrices fill by column. Find the row, then give a vector of columns: m[row, c(...)].

title: Look at the end of the data
body:
Show the last 15 rows of gapminder, then show 5 randomly chosen rows.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
tail(gapminder, n = 15)
gapminder[sample(nrow(gapminder), 5), ]
hint: tail(df, n = 15). For random rows, index with sample(nrow(df), 5).

title: Add a column
body:
Make a new column pop_millions in gapminder with population in millions, then check the first rows.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
gapminder$pop_millions <- gapminder$pop / 1e6
head(gapminder)
hint: Divide the column by 1e6 and assign with gapminder$new_col <-.

title: Subset a data frame
body: Using the built-in mtcars, show the 6-cylinder cars with only the mpg and hp columns, sorted by mpg from highest to lowest.
solution:
six <- mtcars[mtcars$cyl == 6, c("mpg", "hp")]
six[order(-six$mpg), ]
hint: df[rows, c("col1", "col2")], then df[order(-df$mpg), ].

title: Pick row ranges
body:
Create a data frame gapminder_small with only rows 1 through 9 and 19 through 23 of gapminder.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
gapminder_small <- gapminder[c(1:9, 19:23), ]
gapminder_small
hint: Combine two ranges with c(1:9, 19:23) and leave the column index empty.

title: Fix five subsetting bugs
body:
Each line below has a bug. Fix all five so they do what the comment says.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
starter:
# 1. Observations for the year 1957
gapminder[gapminder$year = 1957,]
# 2. All columns except 1 through 4
gapminder[,-1:4]
# 3. Rows where life expectancy is above 80
gapminder[gapminder$lifeExp > 80]
# 4. First row, fourth and fifth columns
gapminder[1, 4, 5]
# 5. Rows for the years 2002 and 2007
gapminder[gapminder$year == 2002 | 2007,]
solution:
gapminder[gapminder$year == 1957, ]
gapminder[, -c(1:4)]
gapminder[gapminder$lifeExp > 80, ]
gapminder[1, c(4, 5)]
gapminder[gapminder$year %in% c(2002, 2007), ]
hint: Look for: assignment instead of comparison, operator precedence with -, a missing comma, a missing c(), and a comparison that isn't repeated.

title: Check before you report
body:
Use an if() statement to print a message saying whether there are any records from 2002 in gapminder. Then do the same for 2012.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
hint: any(gapminder$year == 2002) is a single TRUE/FALSE.

title: Filter and select
body:
With dplyr pipes, produce a data frame with the African values for lifeExp, country and year only. How many rows does it have?

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

year_country_lifeExp_Africa <- gapminder %>%
  filter(continent == "Africa") %>%
  select(year, country, lifeExp)
nrow(year_country_lifeExp_Africa)
hint: filter(continent == "Africa") then select(...).

title: Grouped summary
body:
Summarise mtcars by number of cylinders: the number of cars and the mean mpg rounded to 1 decimal.

    cyl     n mean_mpg
1     4    11     26.7
2     6     7     19.7
3     8    14     15.1
solution:
library(dplyr)

mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_mpg = round(mean(mpg), 1))
hint: group_by(cyl) %>% summarise(n = n(), ...).

title: Longest and shortest lives
body:
Calculate the average life expectancy per country. Then show the countries with the longest and the shortest average.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

lifeExp_bycountry <- gapminder %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarize(mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp))
lifeExp_bycountry %>%
  filter(mean_lifeExp == min(mean_lifeExp) | mean_lifeExp == max(mean_lifeExp))
hint: Summarise by country first, then filter() for the min and max, or arrange() and head(1).

title: Sample within groups
body:
For the year 2002, randomly select 2 countries from each continent and calculate their average life expectancy per continent. Arrange the result with the highest average first.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2002) %>%
  group_by(continent) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 2) %>%
  summarize(mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_lifeExp))
hint: slice_sample(n = 2) after group_by() samples within each group.

title: Long format
body:
Using tidyr, reshape gapminder so pop, lifeExp and gdpPercap are stacked into two columns, obs_type and obs_values. Then calculate the mean of each obs_type for each continent.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

gap_long <- gapminder %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(pop, lifeExp, gdpPercap),
               names_to = "obs_type", values_to = "obs_values")
gap_long %>%
  group_by(continent, obs_type) %>%
  summarize(means = mean(obs_values))
hint: pivot_longer(cols = c(...), names_to = ..., values_to = ...), then group by two columns.

title: Write a function
body: Write a function kelvin_to_celsius() that takes a temperature in Kelvin and returns it in Celsius (subtract 273.15). Test it on 273.15.
hint: Inside the function, compute and return() the value.

title: Coefficient of variation
body:
Write cv(x) that returns the standard deviation divided by the mean, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Print cv() for mtcars$mpg and mtcars$hp.

[1] 30
[1] 46.7
hint: The last expression in a function is its return value.

title: Compose functions
body: Define fahr_to_celsius() by reusing fahr_to_kelvin() and kelvin_to_celsius(). Add a check that stops with an error if temp isn't numeric. Test it on 32.
hint: Call one function inside the other. stopifnot(is.numeric(temp)) checks the input.

title: Vectorised sum
body: Without a loop, compute 1/1² + 1/2² + … + 1/n² for n = 100 and for n = 10,000.
hint: Build the whole vector 1:n, transform it, and sum() it.

title: Loop over groups
body:
Loop over the continents in gapminder and, for each, print whether its mean life expectancy is smaller or larger than 50 years.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
hint: for (cont in unique(gapminder$continent)), subset, take the mean, then if/else.

title: Wrap text
body:
Write fence(text, wrapper) that returns the text vector pasted into one string with wrapper at both ends.

fence(best_practice, "***")
[1] "*** Write programs for people not computers ***"
hint: Add the wrapper to both ends of the vector, then paste(..., collapse = " ").

title: Three-way classification
body:
Loop over each country in gapminder and print whether its mean life expectancy is below 50, between 50 and 70, or above 70.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
hint: if / else if / else inside the loop.

title: Correlation
body: Print the correlation between mpg and wt in mtcars, rounded to 3 decimals.
solution: round(cor(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$wt), 3)
hint: cor(x, y).

title: Two-sample t-test
body: Using the built-in ToothGrowth data, run a t-test comparing tooth len between the two supplement types (supp). Print the t statistic and the p-value, each rounded to 3 decimals.
solution:
res <- t.test(len ~ supp, data = ToothGrowth)
round(res$statistic, 3)
round(res$p.value, 3)
hint: Formula syntax: t.test(len ~ supp, data = ToothGrowth). The result is a list with $statistic and $p.value.

title: Multiple regression
body: Fit a linear model of mpg on wt and hp using mtcars. Print the coefficients rounded to 3 decimals and the R-squared rounded to 3 decimals.
solution:
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
round(coef(fit), 3)
round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 3)
hint: coef(fit) for coefficients; summary(fit)$r.squared for R².

title: Create a data set by hand
body:
Your local animal shelter tracks each dog's Name, Age, Weight, Color and whether it likes Cats. Create work.shelter from the rows below, one line per observation, and print it.

Pluto   3  25  Black    No
Lizzie  10 43  Tan      Yes
Pesci   10 38  Brindle  No
hint: input Name $ Age Weight Color $ Cats $; then datalines;. A length statement stops "Brindle" from being cut to 8 characters.

title: Compute a new variable
body:
Create work.people with name, height_in and weight_lb from the data below. Add bmi = 703 * weight_lb / height_in**2, rounded to 0.1, and print the data set.

Asha 64 130
Bruno 70 185
Cleo 62 115
Dmitri 73 210
hint: Assignment statements go before datalines;. round(x, 0.1).

title: Several records on one line
body:
Create work.shelter2 with the same shelter data, but this time enter all three dogs on a single data line.

Pluto 3 25 Black No Lizzie 10 43 Tan Yes Pesci 10 38 Brindle No
hint: The double trailing @@ holds the line so the next iteration keeps reading from it.

title: Delimited data
body:
Read the #-delimited data below into work.shelter3.

Pluto#3#25#Black#No
Lizzie#10#43#Tan#Yes
Pesci#10#38#Brindle#No
hint: infile datalines dlm='#'; sets the delimiter for in-stream data.

title: Formats and labels
body:
Using the work.class data below:

  1. Use PROC FORMAT to create a format for grade: 0–59 F, 60–69 D, 70–79 C, 80–89 B, 90–100 A.
  2. In a DATA step, label bd as "Birthday", apply your grade format, and format bd with WORDDATE.
  3. Print the table with labels.
hint: proc format; value gradefmt 0-59='F' ...; run;. In the DATA step: label and format grade gradefmt. bd worddate.;. Use proc print ... label;.

title: Average two columns
body:
Create work.cars from sashelp.cars with a new variable mpg_average: the average of MPG_City and MPG_Highway. Print the first five observations of the three variables.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: mean(a, b) or (a + b) / 2. Limit printing with the (obs=5) data set option.

title: Conditional character variable
body:
Add a character variable mpg_quality to work.cars: "Low" when mpg_average is under 20, "Medium" from 20 up to 30, "High" from 30 up. Print observations 65 through 70 for mpg_average and mpg_quality.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: Set length mpg_quality $ 6; first, then if / else if / else. Print a range with (firstobs=65 obs=70).

title: Watch the length
body: Create work.groups from sashelp.class with age_group: "Pre-teen" when age is under 13, otherwise "Teen". Show a frequency table of age_group.
hint: SAS sets a character variable's length from its first value. Declare length age_group $ 8; first.

title: Write a SAS function
body:
Use PROC FCMP to create a function tier with one numeric argument that returns "Low" (under 20), "Medium" (20 to under 30) or "High" (30 and up). Use it to create mpg_quality2 from mpg_average and print observations 65–70.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: function tier(x) $ 6; declares a character return. Point SAS at it with options cmplib=work.functions;.

title: Subset and stack tables
body:
Create sports (Make, Type, MSRP for Sports cars over $100,000) and suv (same columns, SUVs over $60,000). Then row-bind them into expensive and print it. You should get 6 rows.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: keep= and where for each subset. Listing two tables in one SET statement stacks them.

title: One-way frequency table
body:
Generate a frequency table for Type in sashelp.cars. Are the vehicle types evenly distributed?

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: proc freq; tables var; run;

title: Conditional printing
body: From work.class, print student, country and grade for students from France with a grade above 79.
hint: where works inside PROC PRINT. Character comparisons are case-sensitive.

title: Summary by group
body: Using sashelp.class, report N, mean, minimum and maximum of height and weight for each sex, with one decimal place.
hint: Statistics go on the PROC statement with maxdec=1; then class and var.

title: Percentiles to a table
body:
Use PROC MEANS to compute the 10th percentile, median and 90th percentile of MSRP and Horsepower for each Origin. Save the results with ODS OUTPUT as summary_table and print it. Which origin has the highest median price?

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: ods output Summary=work.summary_table; before the PROC captures its Summary table.

title: Query with PROC SQL
body: List the name and age of students in sashelp.class who are 15 or older, oldest first, then by name.
hint: PROC SQL ends with quit;, not run;.

title: Unique levels
body: With PROC SQL, print the unique levels of country in work.class.
hint: select distinct.

title: Group averages
body:
With PROC SQL, show the number of cars and the average MSRP for each Origin in sashelp.cars, formatted as dollars, highest average first.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: avg(MSRP) as avg_msrp format=dollar12. and group by Origin.

title: Store a value in a macro variable
body:
Use PROC SQL to store the median MSRP of sashelp.cars in a macro variable. Then create work.cars with msrp_bin = 1 when MSRP is above the median and 0 otherwise, and show a frequency table of msrp_bin.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: select median(MSRP) into :med_msrp. Reference it as &med_msrp. A comparison like (MSRP > x) evaluates to 1 or 0.

title: Random numbers with a DO loop
body: Create work.rand with 10 observations and two random variables (one normal, one uniform). Use call streaminit with a seed of your choice, and print the data.
hint: Inside do i = 1 to 10; ... output; end;, use rand('normal') and rand('uniform').

title: Nested loops
body: Create a data table with the same two random variables, 10 rows in total: a variable Class that is 1 for the first five rows and 2 for the next five. Drop the inner loop index and add seq running from 1 to 10. Print the data.
hint: Outer loop over Class, inner loop 1 to 5, a counter seq + 1;, and drop=j.

title: PDF and CDF
body: Use a DO loop to create quantiles 0 to 10. For a binomial distribution with p = 0.8 and n = 10, create PDF and CDF. Then use the CDF to create Quantile, which should mirror the loop values. Print the result.
hint: pdf('binomial', q, p, n), cdf(...) and quantile('binomial', prob, p, n).

title: Simulate and plot
body: Create 1,000 random chi-square deviates with 20 degrees of freedom (seed 123). Plot a histogram with PROC SGPLOT using bin width 1, add normal and kernel density curves, the title "My Random Chi-Square Distribution", the x-axis label "Random Chi-Square Deviates", and x-axis limits 5 to 40.
hint: rand('chisquare', 20). In SGPLOT: histogram ... / binwidth=1;, two density statements, and xaxis label= min= max=.

title: Correlation
body: Use PROC CORR to get the correlation between height and weight in sashelp.class.
hint: proc corr; var ...; run;

title: Two-sample t-test
body: Use PROC TTEST to compare mean height between the sexes in sashelp.class.
hint: class names the grouping variable; var the outcome.

title: Multiple regression
body:
Fit a regression of MPG_Highway on Horsepower and Weight using sashelp.cars. Use ODS SELECT to show only the ANOVA, FitStatistics and ParameterEstimates tables, and save predicted values and residuals with an OUTPUT statement.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: ods select ...; before the PROC. In PROC REG: model y = x1 x2; and output out= p= r=;.

title: One-way ANOVA
body:
Use PROC GLM to test whether mean MPG_Highway differs by vehicle Type in sashelp.cars, and request Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons of the means.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: class Type; model y = Type; then lsmeans Type / adjust=tukey pdiff;.
